author: William Quarter (diary); Gilbert J. Garraghan (1921 excerpt)
repository: Internet Archive, item catholicchurchin00garr_0; original diary not inspected
locator: Printed p.127, opening paragraph. Whole page inspected2026-10-23. Exact text:1844,May.The old church is a long,low,frame building,having a small steeple and bell surmounted by a cross. Spacing here normalized; exact typographic punctuation can be reread on the page.

transcribes.work: William Quarter, Diary, entry headed 1844, May:description of the old wooden church and new brick church
transcribes.note: This source records only the period diary excerpt actually printed at Garraghan p.127. The original manuscript has not been inspected. The 1921 page was scan-verified; the 1844 witness text remains mediated through that printing.

what_it_supplies: A period diary description expressly dated May 1844:the old church was long, low, frame, with small steeple, bell and cross. This gives a real later comparison epoch without asserting when the tower was built.
The following 100 x 55 ft dimensions refer to the NEW brick church, not to the old frame church.
what_it_does_not_supply: No exact day in May, no tower installation date, no proof that the tower was absent in 1835.
No number of openings, no old-church dimensions, no metric position or bearing.
No proof that the Moss engraving depicts May 1844 or this exact form of tower.
access_notes: Read a 1921 printed quotation of the diary, not the 1844 manuscript. Keep scan verification of the 1921 printing separate from the transmission status of the original witness text.
